commits.message:
fix(console): delegate printJson to the JSON renderable (rich-json-dxs.1, rich-json-dxs.2)

`Console.printJson` built a key-sorted object and passed it to
`JSON.stringify` as the replacer, behind an `as unknown as undefined`
cast. JSON.stringify ignores a plain object in that position, so
`sortKeys` did nothing, and no highlighter ran. `JSONRenderable` already
did both.

printJson now builds a `JSONRenderable` and prints it with soft wrap, as
Rich's print_json does, so a line wider than the console stays whole and
the output stays valid JSON. Its options are `JSONOptions`, which adds
`highlight`.

json.ts moves from renderables/ to core/. An import from core/console.ts
into renderables/ would have been a third upward edge out of core. The
module imports only core primitives and sits at tier 6 beside pretty, for
the reason pretty.ts's header gives. CLAUDE.md's tier list names it.

The printJson tests expect Python Rich 9d8f9a3's output for key sorting
at every depth and for a line wider than the console, and assert the
theme style Rich gives braces, keys and strings. All three fail against
the old implementation. docs/console.md no longer says printJson does
not colorize.

fix(console): make print honour crop and overflow "ignore" (rich-console-8lg) (#115)

* fix(console): make print honour crop and overflow "ignore" (rich-console-8lg)

`crop` was accepted and never read, and `overflow: "ignore"` was mapped
away before rendering, so it wrapped exactly like "fold".

print now cuts every line at the console width, the line-end included,
unless `crop: false` or `softWrap` turns cropping off. "ignore" reaches
the render as `noWrap`, so the line is neither wrapped nor cut before
that crop. `Segment.cropLines` leaves a space where the edge splits a
wide glyph. Each new test expects the output Python Rich 9d8f9a3 prints
for the same call.

docs/console.md now describes both options, and docs/strip.md no longer
says print leaves a too-wide FlexStrip item whole.

* test(tree, layout): pin wide-glyph cropping to the reference

cropLines now pads a wide glyph the edge cuts through, and Tree labels
and Layout panes both crop through it, so their output changed as well.
Python Rich 9d8f9a3 pads in both places, because render_lines crops
with set_cell_size. These tests assert its rows at width 9, and both
fail against the old no-pad crop.
